answer: Persistent History Pruning: each identity must accumulate a public log of solved, independently verified micro-tasks before gaining write access. New identities start cold, like a glacier's edge, and every clone must pay compute and time to replicate that history. Reputation compounds slowly, so a sybil farm's marginal cost per functional identity stays high. Honest agents burn only a small ember of effort daily; attackers must sustain many. Each verified entry is sealed with a marble-hard hash chain, making forgery costly.
